entries.description: Dependency licensing surveyed across both packages: overwhelmingly MIT/ISC/Apache-2.0/BSD. No infecting copyleft in the application graph.
entries.currentState: Frontend ~420 packages, backend ~480. The only notable items are LGPL-3.0-or-later on sharp's libvips binaries (dynamically linked, redistributed unmodified) and CC-BY-4.0 on caniuse-lite (build-time data).
entries.remediation: Record an attribution/notice file covering LGPL and CC-BY components before external distribution. No license here prevents commercial use.
entries.retestRequirement: Re-run the license survey when dependencies change.

entries.description: Federal regulatory text (29 CFR OSHA, 30 CFR MSHA) is reproduced from eCFR sources.
entries.currentState: Federal regulations are government edicts and are not subject to copyright. Reproduction and redistribution are unproblematic.
entries.remediation: None. Keep the eCFR provenance records with the shipped content.
entries.retestRequirement: Existing source-integrity verifiers.

entries.description: Privately authored consensus standards (ANSI, ASTM, NFPA, ANSI/ASSP) are referenced by NAME AND TOPICAL SCOPE ONLY. No standard text is reproduced anywhere in the shipped product.
entries.currentState: Inspected: entries carry authorityName, a one-line in-house shortUse, an applicability guardrail and reasoning keywords. Titles and citations plus original in-house summaries.
entries.remediation: This is the correct posture and must be PRESERVED as a hard rule. ASTM v. Public.Resource.Org (D.C. Cir. 2023) held that NON-COMMERCIAL posting of incorporated-by-reference standards is fair use; the standards remain copyrighted and that holding does not extend to a COMMERCIAL product redistributing the text. Incorporation by reference does not make private standard text freely redistributable here.
entries.retestRequirement: A content gate asserting no private standard text is ever ingested into shipped content.

entries.description: Fonts, icons and images: the only icon dependency is lucide-react (ISC). No licensed font or stock imagery is bundled.
entries.currentState: No @font-face or Google Fonts import in the shipped layout or stylesheet.
entries.remediation: None. Preserve when brand assets are added.
entries.retestRequirement: Re-check when assets change.

entries.description: SAFETY INSITE is treated as NOT FORMALLY CLEARED. No trademark search, clearance opinion or application is recorded.
entries.currentState: 'InSite' is a common construction/safety-software formative, which raises the likelihood of conflicting commercial use.
entries.evidence: no clearance record in the repository
entries.remediation: Commission a clearance search before external commercialization. A controlled, invitation-only beta under a name later found to conflict is a recoverable but real rebranding cost. Do not rename in this section.
entries.retestRequirement: A recorded clearance opinion.

entries.description: HazLenz has had no conflict or provenance check.
entries.currentState: A coined term, so a priori lower conflict risk than SAFETY INSITE, but unverified.
entries.remediation: Include in the same clearance search as TM-1.
entries.retestRequirement: A recorded clearance opinion.

entries.description: If an operator relies on Safety InSite output as their statutory examination record, the product's retention and export properties become regulatorily significant.
entries.currentState: MSHA 30 CFR 56.18002 requires a competent person designated by the operator to examine each working place each shift, a record made before the end of that shift, and RETENTION FOR ONE YEAR available to the Secretary. OSHA imposes separate recordkeeping duties under 29 CFR 1904. The product neither performs the examination nor guarantees the record.
entries.evidence: ecfr.gov 30 CFR 56.18002; the product has no retention guarantee
entries.remediation: State plainly, in Terms and in product copy, that Safety InSite does not perform the statutory examination and does not itself satisfy any recordkeeping obligation, and that the operator remains responsible for making and retaining required records. Pair with ST-3 to give customers a dependable export.
entries.retestRequirement: A copy audit plus a demonstrated export of a full inspection record.

entries.description: Report revision retention is implemented and proven: every issued revision is retained, byte-identical, downloadable, and marked superseded with a link to its successor.
entries.currentState: Customer-reachable since §286. A superseded artifact is never rewritten.
entries.remediation: None.
entries.retestRequirement: validate:286-reports-and-severity R/C series.

entries.description: The only outbound email is password reset, via Resend, and production refuses to run without PASSWORD_RESET_PROVIDER=resend. All other notifications are in-app database rows with no delivery.
entries.currentState: Assignee notifications on corrective-action status changes are written to the notifications table and never sent anywhere.
entries.remediation: Decide whether the beta needs any outbound notification beyond password reset. If not, ensure no surface implies a user will be emailed when work is assigned to them.
entries.retestRequirement: A copy audit of anything implying notification delivery.

entries.description: project-docs/preservation/v1-beta/ does not exist. There is no build-and-restore guide and no machine-readable release manifest.
entries.currentState: Created at §289: project-docs/preservation/v1-beta/ with SAFETY-INSITE-V1-BETA-BUILD-AND-RESTORE-GUIDE.md and release-manifest.json. The manifest carries every required field. The retired digest 3c2c5974… is NOT used as an integrity assertion; it is recorded only as retired. sourceDigest b1f3bd7e…, applicationSourceDigest 2ce8a1d7…, both with the exact command that recomputes them.
entries.remediation: Create the directory, the guide, and a manifest containing productVersion, gitSha, sourceDigest, hazlenzIdentity, frontendVersion, backendVersion, schemaCompatibilityVersion, migrationHead, nodeVersion, npmVersion, databaseVersion, buildTimestamp, knownLimitations, canonicalDocs and validationEvidence.
entries.retestRequirement: A rebuild from the guide reproducing the recorded digests. Note PV-3: the source digest will reproduce; the ARTIFACT is not provably reproducible while Node is unpinned.

entries.description: The historical digest 3c2c5974... is MISATTRIBUTED and must not be used as a current integrity assertion.
entries.currentState: Exhaustively searched at §283: absent from the working tree, all 17,102 git objects, and all four stashes; no derivation from the frozen baseline reproduces it.
entries.remediation: Use instead: commit 709ee151..., the per-document digests in verification/current/LOCAL-PRODUCT-BASELINE.json, and the §274 successor identity 8c163b31..., which verify:274-successor-identity recomputes from live sources.
entries.retestRequirement: verify:274-successor-identity.

entries.description: No release runbook and no tested rollback procedure exist for either the frontend or the backend.
entries.currentState: The register recorded "no runbook in project-docs/". That was WRONG — DEPLOYMENT-RUNBOOK.md, ROLLBACK-MODEL.md, BACKUP-AND-RESTORE.md and MONITORING.md all existed from §268-§270. What was actually missing is that the runbook was STALE against the candidate: a 3-migration backlog instead of 4, expected schema 1800000021000 instead of 1800000022000, and a backup step written against a Render Postgres instance that does not exist. §289 wrote the candidate-exact successor sequence with rollback decision points for all seven named failure surfaces.
entries.remediation: Write the release runbook (order of operations, backup point, migration step, verification step) and define rollback for each half, including what happens to a migration that has already run.
entries.retestRequirement: Execution of the sequence, which is what turns it from a procedure into a record.
entries.note: Not executed. §289 was forbidden to execute it.

entries.description: No production acceptance procedure is defined: after deploying, nothing states what must be true before a human is allowed to use the system.
entries.currentState: All acceptance to date is local-stack acceptance against a disposable database.
entries.remediation: Define a short post-deploy acceptance: health and readiness, version/SHA match, one real inspection to a generated report, storage round-trip, entitlement boundary, and the operational event stream visible.
entries.retestRequirement: The acceptance executed against the controlled production environment and recorded.

entries.description: The cross-tenant recurrence path is REACHABLE in production, because the outcomes table exists there although no migration creates it.
entries.currentState: Closing a corrective action calls CorrectiveActionsService.recordClosureIntelligence, which calls OutcomeService.recordOutcome, which calls checkRecurrence — a count by category with NO organization or owner scope, whose result sets priorityCode to urgent. The code's own comment says this cannot happen because "NO MIGRATION CREATES THE TABLE ... so the table cannot appear by any other route". §289 read production: the table is there. At Threshold A nobody closes anything, so nothing fires. At Threshold C one customer's action would be escalated on another customer's history.
entries.remediation: Either scope the recurrence query to tenant/workspace and prove both directions (the TI-2 remediation), or decide the outcome loop is deliberately global and make that a stated product position. A third option — dropping the production table to restore the original containment — is a production write and belongs to its own authorised section.
entries.retestRequirement: A two-workspace regression proving same-tenant history CAN influence a recurrence and other-tenant history CANNOT.
entries.note: A second consequence: all §286 and §287 action-closure evidence was gathered against databases WITHOUT this table, so local closure evidence does not represent production closure behaviour.

entries.description: The Neon platform backup retention window and point-in-time-recovery setting are unread.
entries.currentState: Neon's control plane was unreachable from §269 and again from §289 — there is no NEON_* credential in the repository or the environment. The operator-controlled logical backup path is proven twice and does not depend on the console, so this is not a "we have no backups" finding. It is a "we do not know what the platform would give us" finding.
entries.remediation: Read the Neon project's history-retention setting and PITR window from the console and record them. One read.
entries.retestRequirement: A recorded retention window and a recorded PITR window.

entries.description: Two operations documents name the wrong database platform.
entries.currentState: CORRECTED AT §289. BACKUP-AND-RESTORE.md now names Neon, records the §289 backup and content-checksum restore, states the PostgreSQL-17-or-newer client requirement and the direct-endpoint requirement, warns about the collation trap, and points step 3 at the §289 sequence. ROLLBACK-MODEL.md now names Neon, splits BACKUPS_AND_RETENTION into the proven half and the unread half, and covers the fourth migration.
entries.remediation: Correct both documents to name Neon and the operator-controlled pg_dump path. SECTION-289-CONTROLLED-PRODUCTION-DEPLOYMENT.md already states the correction and supersedes the stale step; the base documents still carry the wrong statement.
entries.retestRequirement: A read of both documents showing Neon and the four-migration backlog.
entries.note: Registered as blocking Threshold A because an operator executes the sequence at Threshold A and this is the step that fails them.

entries.description: No Node version is pinned, and the Render runtime Node version cannot be read.
entries.currentState: Neither package declares engines.node; there is no .nvmrc and no .node-version. Vercel is set to 24.x, the §289 build host was v20.20.2, and Render exposes its runtime version through neither its API nor the service's startup output. The preservation guide can therefore promise that the SOURCE reproduces exactly and cannot promise that the ARTIFACT does.
entries.remediation: Add engines.node to both packages and a NODE_VERSION variable on the Render service, then re-read and record the runtime version.
entries.retestRequirement: A recorded Render runtime Node version matching a pin in the repository.

entries.description: NEXT_PUBLIC_DISABLE_AUTH is scoped to the Vercel PRODUCTION environment.
entries.currentState: STRUCTURALLY INERT TODAY, and registered anyway. Every consumer either tests NODE_ENV !== "production" directly (AppShell.tsx:3, lib/auth.ts:113, lib/billing.ts isLocalDevAuthBypass) or delegates to getLocalDevPlanCode(), whose first line returns "free" when NODE_ENV === "production". So the variable does nothing in a production build whatever its value. The hazard is the next consumer who reads the variable without the guard.
entries.remediation: Remove it from the Production scope. It has no effect there, so removal is behaviour-preserving.
entries.retestRequirement: An environment-scope listing showing it absent from Production.
entries.note: This is a P2 because of what it invites, not because of what it does. Do not restate it as a live auth bypass.

entries.description: Five verification instruments are stale against the §285-§288 successor.
entries.currentState: check:launch-pricing fails 1 of 39 on an allowlist that predates the Expert HazLenz surface — it conflates the retired Expert PRICING TIER (correctly purged; all three price checks pass) with Expert HazLenz the CAPABILITY. check:company-actions and check:action-workflow wait for a heading the command-center no longer renders and need VAL_EMAIL/VAL_PASSWORD. check:closure-inspection-workspace expects ports 3100/4200. check:phase5-inspection-report-release calls a HazLenz route that answers 404. validate:279-update-delivery needs a seeded account.
entries.remediation: Update each instrument to the successor product. §289 deliberately did NOT edit any allowlist or assertion to make a gate pass.
entries.retestRequirement: Each instrument running and reporting a result rather than an environment error.
entries.note: NOT product defects. No instrument in this list reported a defect in the product; each failed to run, or failed against its own stale expectation.

thresholdCountRule: A threshold's blocker count is the number of entries whose blocksThresholdX flag is set. Closing an entry clears its flags and records what it used to block in wasBlockingThresholds, so the entry is never deleted and the count never counts a closed item.
candidateHeadNote: The release SHA is the branch tip at push time and CANNOT be recorded inside the commit that would record it — each such commit changes the value. So the release is bound by a digest instead of by a SHA, which is the stronger binding in any case: the SHA to deploy is whatever origin/beta/expert-hazlenz-validated-candidate-2026-09-12 points at after step 1, PROVIDED its applicationSourceDigest equals 2ce8a1d7b045818cb9708af9414fe8d189523e334dad955b617268cc932f2618. Verify that before deploying; it is one command.
